headline: Green candles, red trend lines: every major still trades under its 200-day average
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it overrides everything else today. All seven assets on the board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sit below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. BTC is 48.1% off its 12-month high, ETH is down 60.1%, SOL 69.9%, XRP 67.3%, BNB 54.8%, DOGE 75.6%, and ADA the furthest out at 82.3%. That's a uniform picture: seven for seven below trend. A single green day, and today is green (total market cap up 1.44%, BTC up 1.23%), doesn't change a structural regime like that. Bounces happen inside downtrends all the time; the 200-day line just tells you which one you're in.

Momentum tells a more split story than trend does. RSI-14 readings cluster in the high-40s to low-60s, nothing overbought or oversold, which reads as a market resting rather than trending hard in either direction. MACD is where the divergence shows up: BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP all sit below their signal lines (momentum still fading), while BNB, DOGE, and ADA have flipped above theirs. ADA is the standout, up 5.1% on the day with 74.7% 30-day realized volatility, easily the most violent mover among the majors. So you have a trend-following majority (BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP) still losing momentum underneath a below-trend structure, and a smaller group of alts (BNB/DOGE/ADA) picking up bullish momentum while still trapped under their own 200-day lines. Worth naming as a divergence rather than papering over it.

Positioning backs up the idea that today's rally was built partly on squeezed shorts. Funding is positive everywhere on the leverage board, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets: BTC at 8.2% annualized, XRP at 8.7%, SOL at 5.4%, DOGE at 4.6%, ETH the cheapest at 2.1%. Long/short account ratios lean heavily long, especially in DOGE (3.76) and XRP (3.04), so the crowd on these venues is stacked on one side of the boat. The 24-hour liquidation data shows who got hurt: BTC shorts lost $3.91m versus $584k in longs, ETH shorts lost $8.72m versus $1.43m in longs. That's a short squeeze pattern, not fresh conviction buying, and it sits on top of real size, BTC open interest is near $1.99B, ETH near $1.37B.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. Whale wallets moved a net $112.7m onto exchanges over the past 24 hours, BTC specifically, with $193.7m flowing in (the single biggest transfer landing at Kraken) against $80.98m flowing out (from Binance). Moving coin onto an exchange is usually a precursor to selling, not holding. Against that, there's $180.8m of stablecoin buying power sitting on the sidelines, though the stablecoin float itself is down 1.59% over the past 30 days to $304.6B, so the dry powder pile is shrinking, not growing. The four-session weekly net whale flow (+$904.1m, -$96.8m, -$244.3m, +$1,071.3m) shows no settled direction, it's whipping both ways. On the ETF side, BTC funds printed a positive $32.1m net inflow on 29 Jul 2026, but that single day breaks from a five-session net of -$494.4m, and same_direction_days of 1 confirms it was an outlier day against the recent run. ETH ETFs were negative both on the day (-$32.9m) and over five sessions (-$56.2m). So the daily print and the five-day trend disagree for BTC, and that gap is the honest read: one green day of ETF flow sitting inside a five-day outflow stretch.

Sentiment is the foil here. The Fear & Greed Index reads 28, still labeled Fear, sitting near the upper edge of its own 30-day range of 11 to 33. So the crowd feels cautious even as price ticks up, funding stays positive, and shorts get liquidated. That's not a contradiction so much as a snapshot of a market where sentiment lags the tape, or where the tape is a short squeeze the sentiment gauge hasn't been fooled by. What's worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF net flips positive to confirm the single-day print, whether whale flow direction reverses from onto-exchanges toward off-exchanges, and whether any major asset actually reclaims its 200-day average rather than just bouncing beneath it.
